physical_harm: Two persons died and others sustained injuries
number_of_offences: Two counts charged and both upheld
premeditation_planning: The court found premeditation/planning due to enmity and weapon use
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the testimony of PWs 1, 3 and 4, and the evidence of the eye-witnesses, along with the post-mortem reports and ballistic evidence, as credible and unshaken.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that despite lengthy cross-examination, the accused were not able to bring any point shaking their credibility.
bail_history: Appellant is on bail. His bail bonds are cancelled.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 05.11.1974; Trial judgment: 31.03.1981; High Court decision: 17.12.2004; Supreme Court decision: 01.09.2015
legal_representation: Salman Khurshid, lmtiaz Ahmed, Naghma lmtiaz (for Equity Lex Associates) for the Appellant; Ratnakar Dash, Harsh Vardhan Jha, Adarsh Upadhyay for the Respondent
investigation_status: Case registered in Crime Case No. 313/1974; charge sheet filed on 07.01.1975
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction and sentence; High Court: Affirmed conviction and partly allowed appeal; Supreme Court: Dismissed appeal
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant and the accused party were having enmity against the deceased due to a civil suit and contempt petition. They were armed with guns and lathis, and the appellant fired a gunshot resulting in the death of Abbas Khan. The prosecution also emphasized that the evidence of the three eye-witnesses remained unshaken and that the accused were not able to shake the credibility of these witnesses.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the appellant and the accused were not the aggressors, and the incident took place near the chabutra of Shafiq Khan. They contended that the deceased Abbas Khan and lsrar were armed with guns and pistols, and the prosecution failed to explain the recovery of the gun and the absence of blood at the alleged location of the incident.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that when a gun is used, the person firing the gun must be presumed to have knowledge and intention that the injury inflicted is sufficient to cause death, thereby constituting murder.
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed due to the magnitude of the crime and the proportionality of punishment, with the court emphasizing that the manner in which the offence was committed warranted a proper sentence.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The court considered the enmity between the accused and the deceased, the use of a gun, and the fact that two persons died and several others were injured as aggravating factors.
other_sentence_order: The court cancelled the appellant's bail bonds and ordered him to be taken into custody to serve the remaining sentence.
